_meta.indication: TORISEL is indicated for the treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, multi-center, three-arm, randomized, open-label study comparing interferon alfa (IFN) alone, temsirolimus 25 mg alone, and the combination of temsirolimus 15 mg plus IFN.
pivotal_trials.population: Previously untreated patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma who had 3 or more of 6 poor prognostic factors.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall survival (OS), the prespecified primary endpoint.
pivotal_trials.n: 626 randomized: IFN alone (n=207), temsirolimus 25 mg (n=209), temsirolimus 15 mg + IFN (n=210).
pivotal_trials.result: Median OS 10.9 months with temsirolimus 25 mg vs 7.3 months with IFN; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.58, 0.92); p=0.0078. The combination (temsirolimus 15 mg + IFN) HR vs IFN was 0.96 (95% CI 0.76, 1.20) and did not significantly improve survival.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=30%) are rash, asthenia, mucositis, nausea, edema, and anorexia. In the randomized trial (TORISEL n=208): rash 97 (47%), asthenia 104 (50%), mucositis 86 (41%), nausea 77 (37%), edema 73 (35%). Serious risks include hypersensitivity reactions, hyperglycemia, interstitial lung disease, bowel perforation, and acute renal failure.
target_moa: Temsirolimus is an inhibitor of mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin); it binds the intracellular protein FKBP-12, and the protein-drug complex inhibits mTOR activity controlling cell division, producing G1 growth arrest in treated tumor cells.
modality: Small molecule (kinase/mTOR inhibitor) given as intravenous infusion.

summary.text: Temsirolimus (Torisel) for advanced renal cell carcinoma had Fast Track status and was granted regular (not accelerated) approval under Priority review, based on a statistically significant overall survival improvement in a single randomized phase 3 trial; no advisory committee was convened.
